flows.summary: List every entry point the target repo exposes so independent passes have a shared join key.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap inventory` to discover every entry point via the configured or auto-detected adapters
steps.notes: In this repo only the cli adapter runs (flowmap.toml); fastapi/rails/nextjs adapters' entries() are reached the same way via the ADAPTERS dict for other stacks.

flows.summary: Generate briefs for independent mapping passes and check each pass's output for invented citations and missing entry points.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap brief <run-id> <method>` to write a filled-in brief for one agent pass
steps.notes: Template text comes from flowmap/RUN_SPEC.md (first 3 lines dropped); the agent then writes docs/flowmap/runs/<run-id>.json outside any entry point.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap verify` to reject bad citations and unplaced inventory entry points in a pass's JSON
steps.notes: Read-only; exit code 1 on any BAD/MISS.

flows.summary: Vote the independent passes into one map and surface the disagreements a human must decide.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap reconcile` to merge pass outputs into map.json, MAP.md and QUESTIONS.md by endpoint agreement
steps.notes: Reads decisions.json (endpoint_flow pins, confirmed_steps) and config.flow_order() at import time.

steps.name: Maintainer names proposed flows in flowmap.toml, pins answers in decisions.json, and re-runs reconcile
steps.notes: flowmap.toml and decisions.json are hand-edited; no command writes them. canonical_new_flows strips `new:` once the human adopts the id.

flows.summary: Render the consensus map as Mermaid diagrams and an interactive HTML atlas to see flows, steps and shared code.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap diagrams` to write Mermaid diagrams at system, flow and step zoom
steps.notes: Requires map.json and inventory.json from earlier commands.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap atlas` to build the interactive HTML map and browses flows, steps and code flow in it

flows.summary: Place a PR or symbol change on the flow map: which flows/steps it touches, what can reach it, and what code is off-map.

steps.name: Reviewer runs `flowmap lens <base> <head>` to see flows/steps touched, endpoint changes, call-graph reach and off-map code
steps.notes: Prints markdown to stdout; the pr-lens skill consumes it. Builds the inventory at both git revisions via a reader with a .ref attribute.

steps.name: Reviewer runs `flowmap atlas --pr base..head=label` to paint a change's direct and reached steps onto the atlas
Reviewer runs `flowmap callgraph impact <file:sym>` to list which entry points and flows can reach a symbol
steps.notes: Without the `impact` subcommand it just prints definition/edge counts. Not mentioned in README's workflow, only in bin/flowmap help.

observations: Two implementations of 'which symbols did this diff change': flowmap/lens.py:main (keeps <module>, tracks new_symbols vs base) and flowmap/atlas.py:overlay (drops <module>, splits new/changed) each re-derive it from flowmap/lens.py:changed_lines + flowmap/lens.py:symbols_at, and each rebuilds a head-revision flowmap/callgraph.py:Graph.__init__ separately.

flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes reads split votes back out of the human-facing QUESTIONS.md with a regex instead of from map.json; the data written by flowmap/reconcile.py:write_questions_md becomes an implicit machine format.
flowmap/atlas.py:overlay calls flowmap/lens.py:endpoint_set(head) twice, each re-running the whole inventory over git show.

Stale/mismatched prose baked into outputs: flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.write always prints '**workflow engine** = `executor.run_workflow`' and says plumbing is overridden in decisions.json, while plumbing actually comes from flowmap.toml via flowmap/config.py:load; flowmap/reconcile.py:write_map_md cites 'tools/flowmap/reconcile.py'; callgraph's docstring still says 'backend/app'.
flowmap/callgraph.py:Graph.reaches has no callers in the repo (dead code).
Importing flowmap/atlas.py pulls in flowmap/lens.py, whose module-level code compiles regexes from flowmap/config.py:app_dirs, so even a plain atlas build depends on lens's config side effects.

flowmap/verify.py:anchor_ok treats any line matching `^\s*name\s*[:=(]` as a definition, so a local assignment or a call at line start satisfies a citation; verification is looser than 'defined in that file'.

Nothing writes flowmap.toml or decisions.json; the human decision step between two reconcile runs is entirely off-CLI, and flowmap/callgraph.py:endpoint_flows and flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.__init__ fail outright if map.json does not yet exist.
